accept: perimembranous ventricular septal defect with left heart volume overload

echoTasks.find: Dropout of the perimembranous septum with left to right colour flow across it
High velocity left to right jet on continuous wave Doppler confirming a restrictive gradient
Dilated left atrium and left ventricle from volume overload with normal pulmonary pressure

auscultation.added: Palpable thrill at the left lower sternal edge
auscultation.murmur: Harsh pansystolic murmur grade 4 of 6 at the left lower sternal edge without radiation

exam.general: Alert 8 month old girl, mild tachypnoea, sweaty forehead during feeds, weight below the third centile
exam.jvp: Difficult to assess in an infant, no hepatojugular reflux sought
exam.other: Liver palpable 2 cm, subcostal recession while feeding, no cyanosis
exam.precordium: Hyperdynamic precordium with a systolic thrill at the left lower sternal edge
exam.pulse: Bounding 132, good volume, femoral pulses present and equal

history.a: Poor weight gain, tires during feeds needing frequent pauses, breathes fast
history.q: What worries the mother about feeding and growth

history.a: Two episodes of fast breathing with fever, treated as pneumonia at the primary centre
Full term normal delivery, cried at birth, no blue spells
history.q: Birth history and any blue spells

history.a: First child, parents healthy, no consanguinity
Exclusive breastfeeding plus family foods started at six months
Mother is a homemaker, father is a mason, smoke free home

keyPoints: Optimise feeds with small frequent high energy feeds and monitor weight on a growth chart
Treat intercurrent chest infections early and give all due vaccines including influenza where available
Refer to paediatric cardiology for elective surgical closure assessment, as moderate defects with failure to thrive seldom close alone
Counsel the parents that the murmur is from extra lung flow, and that endocarditis precautions apply before dental work
Review monthly for pulmonary pressure rise, falling murmur intensity, or a second heart sound that turns single and loud
management.model: Nutritional support with infection vigilance and referral to paediatric cardiology for closure assessment

stem: An 8 month old girl from a village near Lucknow is brought for poor weight gain and breathlessness during feeds. She had two treated chest infections. A harsh pansystolic murmur with a thrill is heard at the left lower sternal edge, and the precordium is hyperdynamic.
teaching: A harsh pansystolic murmur with a thrill at the left lower sternal edge in a thriving poor infant points to a ventricular septal defect
Failure to thrive with feeding diaphoresis is heart failure in infancy, not poor milk alone
Moderate defects volume load the left heart while pressure stays normal, which is why the child is pink
Monthly review watches for pulmonary hypertension, the complication that changes the plan
title: Ventricular septal defect in an infant with failure to thrive
